2. At the very outset, it is relevant to mention here that charge sheet was filed against three accused persons, namely, Shobhraj, Rajendra and Khunni but accused Rajendra was exonerated from the charges levelled against him.

3. This criminal appeal has been preferred by appellants challenging the impugned judgment and order dated 10.09.2002 passed by learned Additional District & Sessions Judge (Fast Track Court No. 4), Sitapur in Sessions Trial No. 420 of 2000, arising out of Case Crime No. 49 of 1995 whereby accused appellant no. 1 has been convicted and sentenced to undergo two years and six month Shobharaj And Another vs State Of U.P. on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171222859/

sentences.text: In default of payment of fine, he has to undergo further three months simple imprisonment.
Further appellant no. 2 was convicted and sentenced under Section 324/34 IPC for two years and six months rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs.2,000/-/
In default of payment of fine, he has to undergo further three months simple imprisonment.

4. In short the prosecution case is that FIR of this case was lodged by Vijay Kumar scribed by Om Prakash with the allegation that on 16.3.1995 at about 9:00 p.m. some altercation took place with accused Shobhraj.
Due to this reason, accused Shobhraj and Rajendra armed with country-made pistol and accused Khunni armed with lathi arrived at his door and hurled abuses.
When he stopped abusing then Shobhraj and Rajendra with intention to commit murder opened fire.
On this scuffle sister-in-law (Bhabhi) of complainant Vijay Kumar received bullet injury.
This incident was seen by Ramesh Gokaran and Vijay Kumar.
The accused persons were identified in the light of lantern.
5. On the basis of written report lodged on 17.3.1995 at 3:30 pm., Case Crime No. 49 of 1995 under Sections 307 and 504 IPC was registered at Police Station Mahmudabad, District Sitapur.
6. The Investigation of this case was conducted by Investigating Officer S.I. Brij Raj Yadav, who inspected the spot, prepared site plan and recorded the statements of witnesses.
The Investigating Officer after due investigation and completion of investigation, submitted charge sheet against accused Shobhraj, Rajendra and Khunni under Sections 307 and 504 IPC.
After committal, the charge was framed against appellant Shobhraj under Sections 307 and 504 IPC and for the offence under Section 307/34 and 504 the charge was framed against Khunni and Rajendra.
The same was read-over to appellants in Hindi, they denied the charges levelled against them and claimed to be tried.

7. The prosecution in order to prove its case has examined PW-1 complainant Vijay Kumar, who is the injured witness, PW-2 Sushma Devi, PW-3 Vijay Kumar son of Parashuram, PW-4 S.I. Brij Raj Yadav, who is the Investigating Officer of this case, PW-5 Dr. K.P. Sinha.
Thus the prosecution relied upon oral evidence of PW-1 to PW4.

The prosecution also relied upon documentary evidence, such as, written report Ex. Ka-1 proved by PW-1 Vijay Kumar, site plan Ex. Ka-2, charge sheet Ex. Ka-3,
FIR Ex. Ka-4 Nakal G.D. Ex. Ka-5 and injury report of Vijay Kumar Ex. Ka-6, injury report of Sushma Devi Ex. Ka-7.

Thus the prosecution has relied upon oral evidence of PW-1 to PW-5 and as a documentary evidence Ex. Ka-1 to Ex. Ka-6.
8.

The statement of the accused appellants were recorded under Section 313 Cr.P.C. wherein they denied the charge levelled against them and stated that all the witnesses are falsely deposing against them on account of enmity.
The Investigating Officer done wrong investigation.
They have been falsely implicated in this but the accused persons failed to adduce any evidence in defence.

9. The trial court after considering the statements of witnesses, evidence available on record, came to the conclusion that the prosecution has been successful to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt against the accused appellants and accused Rajendra was acquitted but no State Appeal has been filed against accused Rajendra.

2 10.
Learned counsel for appellants has vehemently argued that findings of the guilt recorded by the trial court are not based on correct facts available on record.
Further submission is that the identification of the appellants is doubtful as the incident alleged to have taken place in the night hours and there was no sufficient source of light.
Some unknown persons inflicted injuries to the injured and due to parti-bandi and the trial court without appreciating the evidence available on record has wrongly convicted the appellants.

11. Lastly it has been argued that the incident relates to the year 1995 since then around 28 years have passed and both the parties are living happily in the village and no untoward incident has ever occurred between them.

Since the incident had taken place about 28 years ago, therefore, learned counsel for appellants has submitted that leniency may be given to the appellants as no fruitful purpose would be served by sending the appellants to jail again.
Sending the appellants in jail would give rise to enmity again between the parties.

12. Learned A.G.A. for the State, while refuting the submission of learned counsel for appellants, has submitted that the finding of guilt recorded by the trial court are based on correct appreciation of evidence available on record.
The prosecution has fully supported the prosecution case and there are no contradictions in the statements of the witnesses, therefore, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

13. During course of argument, learned counsel for appellants has submitted that the interest of justice would suffice, if appellants are sentenced to the period already undergone by them and enhancing the fine.

Further learned counsel for appellants submitted that though there are sufficient reason to challenge the judgment on merits yet they are restricting the challenge to non-consideration of the applicability of provision contained in Section 4 of Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 (in short "Probation Act") .

(1) When any person is found guilty of having committed an offence not punishable with death or imprisonment for life and the court by which the person is found guilty is of opinion that, having regard to the circumstances of the case including the nature of the offence and the character of the offender, it is expedient to release him on probation of good conduct, then, notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, the court may, instead of sentencing him at once to any punishment direct that he be released on his entering into a bond, with or without sureties, to appear and receive sentence when called upon during such period, not exceeding three years, as the court may direct, and in the meantime to keep the peace and be of good behaviour:
Provided that the court shall not direct such release of an offender unless it is satisfied that the offender or his surety, if any, has a fixed place of abode or regular occupation in the place over which the court exercises jurisdiction or in which the offender is likely to live during the period for which he enters into the bond.
(2) Before making any order under sub-section (1), the court shall take into consideration the report, if any, of the probation officer concerned in relation to the case.
(3) When an order under sub-section (1) is made, the court may, if it is of opinion that in the interests of the offender and of the public it is expedient so to do, in addition pass a supervision order directing that the offender shall remain under the supervision of a probation officer named in the order during such period, not being less than one year, as may be specified therein, and may in such supervision order impose such conditions as it deems necessary for the due supervision of the offender.
(4) The court making a supervision order under sub-section (3) shall require the offender, before he is released, to enter into a bond, with or without sureties, to observe the conditions specified in such order and such additional conditions with respect to residence, abstention from intoxicants or any other matter as the court may, having regard to the particular circumstances, consider fit to impose for preventing a repetition of the same offence or a commission of other offences by the offender.
(5) The court making a supervision order under sub-section (3) shall explain to the offender the terms and conditions of the order and shall forthwith furnish one copy of the supervision order to each of the offenders, the sureties, if any, and the probation officer concerned.

15. There are other legislative requirements that need to be kept in mind.
The Probation of Offenders Act provides, in Section 5 thereof for payment of compensation to the victim of a crime (as does Section 357 of the Code of Criminal Procedure).

Yet, additional changes were brought about in the Code of Criminal Procedure in 2006 providing for a victim compensation scheme and for additional rights to the victim of a crime, including the right to file an appeal against the grant of inadequate compensation.
How often have the Courts used these provisions?

16. In Ankush Shivaji Gaikwad v. State of Maharashtra MANU/SC/0461/2013: (2013) 6 SCC 770 and Jitendra Singh v. State of U.P. MANU/SC/0679/2013 : (2013) 11 SCC 193 the Court held that consideration of grant of compensation to the victim of a crime is mandatory, in the following words taken from Ankush Shivaji Gaikwad:
"While the award or refusal of compensation in a particular case may be within the court's discretion, there exists a mandatory duty on the court to apply its mind to the question in every criminal case.

opennyai_summary.decision:
In the present appeal fine of Rs.2,000/- each has been imposed by the trial court on the appellants.
Thus the appeal is partly allowed.
The conviction as directed by trial court is confirmed under Section 324 IPC and is directed to be released on probation under Section 4 of the U.P. 19. Considering the law propounded by Hon'ble Apex Court and as per provisions of Section 357 Cr.P.C., I am of the view that compensation should be awarded to the victim's family.
20. Therefore, fine of Rs.2,000/- each is enhanced to Rs.7,000/- each, which shall be deposited before the trial court.

If injured Vijay Kumar and Smt. Sushma Devi is not alive, the same shall be given to their legal heirs and Rs. 2,000/- each shall be deposited in State exchequer.
It is made clear that if the appellants fail to pay aforesaid amount then, they shall undergo imprisonment and sentence as directed by they trial court.
One month's time is granted to appellants to deposit the fine as mentioned by this Court.
The appellants are on bail.
They need not to surrender.
21. One month's time is provided to the appellants to deposit fine amount from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.
22. Thus, the appeal is dismissed on the point of conviction and partly allowed on the point of sentence.
